headline: High: n8n can write shared files and execute commands while OpenHands has broad shell, browser, and filesystem access, creating dangerous default interaction paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: n8n can emit workflow outputs and write to the server filesystem, while OpenHands can read mounted files and act on them in its runtime. That creates a plausible file-based instruction bridge even without clipboard or MCP. The pathway is not provably blocked, but it is not inherently a raw shared-channel hijack either.
conditions: IF n8n writes attacker-controlled text into a file that OpenHands later reads as instructions, injection is possible.
IF OpenHands is configured to follow file contents as task context, the risk materializes.
mitigations: Separate the two agents onto different directories.
Require manual review of any file passed from n8n to OpenHands.
Use a strict file schema for handoffs.
Disable automatic ingestion of arbitrary text files.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: n8n touches whatever the workflow processes and can access server files plus broad egress; OpenHands touches files in its runtime sandbox and can also use broad egress. If sensitive data lands in a shared workspace or is forwarded through either agent, both can expose it beyond the local boundary. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace by default, so medium is the higher justified level.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same sensitive files or workspace, leakage risk increases.
IF either agent forwards file contents to external APIs, sensitive data can leave the environment.
mitigations: Keep sensitive inputs out of shared folders.
Restrict outbound network destinations for both runtimes.
Use separate credentials and secrets stores.
Redact secrets before handoff between agents.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: n8n has server filesystem write and command execution, and OpenHands has filesystem write, shell, package install, and git modification inside its runtime. The profiles show overlapping mutable capabilities with no locking or coordination primitive, so concurrent writes or state corruption are plausible in default multi-instance use. Uncertainty about the exact shared boundary escalates rather than lowers severity.
conditions: IF both agents target the same mounted directory or repository, write conflicts can occur.
IF either agent runs concurrently without external locking, state corruption is possible.
mitigations: Assign disjoint working directories.
Serialize writes with a lock file.
Avoid shared git repositories.
Run one agent at a time for mutable tasks.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n can generate workflow outputs and trigger downstream actions, while OpenHands can execute shell, browser, and filesystem operations. If OpenHands consumes n8n output as task input without verification, an error or malicious instruction can cascade into real actions. The pair therefore has an action-taking chain with no documented verification barrier in the profiles.
conditions: IF OpenHands treats n8n-produced text as authoritative task context, cascading errors can propagate.
IF n8n triggers OpenHands actions without a human review step, downstream harm can occur.
mitigations: Insert a human approval step before execution.
Require structured outputs from n8n.
Validate OpenHands inputs against a schema.
Log and diff all handoff artifacts.
requires-engineering: add policy checks before any destructive action.

E_compliance.rationale: n8n handles per-credential secrets on its server and processes whatever the workflow touches, while OpenHands handles model-provider API keys and files in its runtime sandbox. If regulated data is routed through both, retention and residency obligations can diverge across two separate systems. The profiles do not specify matching compliance controls, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed by both agents, retention and logging mismatches can arise.
IF one environment stores secrets or artifacts longer than the other, compliance drift occurs.
mitigations: Minimize regulated data in both systems.
Align retention settings before use.
Review where secrets are stored and logged.
Use separate environments for regulated workloads.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls end-to-end.
